Alright, let me think this through. I'm 64, farmed these fields for 40 years. 19.1 mu total — I keep about 13 mu in the wheat-maize rotation on the better flat ground, and 6.1 mu out on the western piece where cotton does okay. Household's six people but my son works in town and my daughter-in-law's at the factory, so really it's me, my wife, and the two grandkids when school's out. Got the well and a submersible pump.

**Wheat (already in the ground since last October).** Put down about 35 kg of the 15-15-15 compound per mu at planting, usual thing. Now it's jointing time — I'll topdress urea, maybe 10-11 kg/mu. Extension guy at the township said 8 is enough but I've always done a bit more, wheat never lies to you. Going to irrigate at jointing this week, then again at grain filling. Third watering only if May stays dry. Expecting around 450 kg/mu if the wind doesn't flatten it.

**Cotton (planting now, mid-late April).** Buying seed from the same shop in town — improved variety, not the expensive Bt one, my piece isn't that bollworm-heavy. Cotton's a headache on labor, the picking kills my back now, but prices held up last year so I'm keeping it. Fertilizer lighter than wheat, maybe 12 kg N split between base and flowering. Will need to spray — aphids early, bollworms in July, and I always do one fungicide before rains. My wife and I pick what we can, hire two village women for two weeks in September.

**Maize (planting mid-June, right after wheat harvest).** Tight window, one week maybe. I hire the combine for wheat and the no-till planter comes right behind — 50 yuan/mu for the planter, worth every fen at my age. Denghai hybrid seed, what everyone around here uses. Base fertilizer at planting, topdress urea at big trumpet stage about 8-10 kg. One irrigation at tasseling if July's dry. Autumn rains usually carry it. Around 500 kg/mu is what I get most years.

Cash is always tight at planting time. I'm not going to overspend on inputs — at my age I don't need to push for record yields, I need steady harvests.
